decision.title: The book teaches with five projects of one story (packet book-5)

body.p: , after , , , . The owner: restructure the book around useful examples (structured specifications kept in XML, creating and transforming SVG, SCXML annotated with data schemas and XHTML, a diff of call chains through the tree-sitter bridge, a diff of OTel traces before and after a change) instead of the library/loans data. The plan is docs/tasks/book.md; this record keeps the choices later packets must not reopen.

item.p: One story. The five projects belong to one made-up system, Latch (door locks, a controller, services): the draft's requirement anchors are what the machine's latch:implements names, the code change of call-chains is the change the traces record, and one diagram vocabulary draws services, the machine and both diffs.

Project directories are example directories. docs/book/examples/ gains spec, svg, scxml, call-chains and traces; every chapter file that uses a project names its directory in <!-- examples: -->, so a reader runs a project's commands from one place. Their seed files (committed by book-5) are frozen during the rewrite; packets add files under names the plan gives them, never list a project root, and reach another project's file through a relative symlink (check-book-examples.sh's copytree follows it). Rejected: per-chapter directories with copies of the data (copies drift) and a multi-directory examples: comment (readers could not run the commands from one directory).

The spec is xml2rfc v3, a subset (RFC 7991 and the RFC Editor's current grammar, no namespace), not an own vocabulary: it is what IETF authors write and xml2rfc renders it. Requirements are anchored t paragraphs with bcp14; anchors are names given once (not in document order), the renderer numbers by position; anchors are checked with xs:unique and xs:keyref, not xs:ID. Two drafts, -00 and -01, so a requirement diff by anchor works.

SCXML: SCXML 1.0 with datamodel="ecmascript"; the self-description is in urn:example:latch (event declarations with payload element names, latch:type on data, latch:implements, XHTML in states), checked by a subset of the Recommendation's schema (one target per transition, so a keyref can check it) importing latch-data.xsd. The seed machine has four flaws that are valid XSD but found by the schema-aware checks.

Structure: 18 chapters, seven of them projects; the three languages are taught on the spec, each ending with a project section; SVG follows XSLT, the SCXML project follows XSD, call chains come before traces. Windows move from the XQuery chapter to the traces project, streaming from the XSLT chapter to it, and the codegen project and the iXML part stay (plus one ABNF task).

Packets: book-6 to book-12 rewrite in parallel, each owning its chapter files and the example files it adds; book-13 then owns SUMMARY.md, the introduction, the appendices and every "Chapter N" text (cross references are by title meanwhile).

Verified: release build of HEAD: both drafts and the machine validate; broken copies give the expected cvc codes; the ten TypeScript files parse without ERROR nodes; json-doc reads 16 and 30 spans; sketch queries give the call-chain diff and the trace diff the plan states (lock-service to lock-registry 1 -> 5 on GET /doors, a new audit-service, no door-cache).
